INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED claim j6o1rx coefficient (Table 5 Erickson-Whited): errors-in-variables higher-order-moment slope = m(xy^2)/m(x^2 y) = 0.50728, matching published 0.507 (SE 0.014 from the supplied Stata log = 0.5072804/0.014008). The SE depends on the external EWreg.ado implementation the human located externally.

Claim q7w3nr (68% are types 3 or 4 = alpha<rho) reproduces only APPROXIMATELY: shipped posterior columns classify 70/101 = 69.31% as types 3 or 4 (argmax rule, and early_post>0.5 agree). Paper main text says 68%, but the paper's own Table 4 fractions (0.407+0.288) sum to 69.5% - an internal inconsistency in the paper.

Reproducibility/robustness caveat: the finite-mixture posterior-probability columns (type1-4_post) that drive every Table 5 regression are AUTHOR-SUPPLIED in STATA_data.xlsx and are NOT regenerated by the shipped MATLAB code (quick_estimates.m writes no Excel; make_boots.m/generalized_EMscript_forboots.m fail on xlswrite platform dependency and only ran after human code fixes; STATA commands.do has hardcoded author paths and a missing EWreg dependency). All four claim-level NUMBERS nevertheless reproduce exactly/approximately from the shipped analysis file.

Found a cross-file data inconsistency (F1): subject 5-16 is coded choice=1 (early) in STATA_data.xlsx but resolution=3 (indifferent) in raw inputs.xls; the 'early' regression DV sums to 60 while the paper's descriptive '61 of 101' counts choice==1. The paper's 61 matches the analysis file, not the raw inputs.

Agrees with the human FLoRA 'computational issues' verdict: the reproduction pipeline is NOT push-button (platform-dependent Excel I/O, hardcoded paths, missing EWreg dependency, regression inputs not re-generated from code). Yet, consistent with the human SCORE trail (which rated claims pp36jq/x64975/j6o1rx as reproduced and q7w3nr approximate), the headline numerical claims are recoverable from the shipped data.
